effort.name: Sample Co
effort.description: Fictional benefits-administration platform used to illustrate the dashboard

chair.rationale: Employer benefits administration sold through resellers and platform partners; core sector.

roster.name: Channel partner
roster.rationale: Reseller commentary and partner announcements available.
roster.view: The product quotes cleanly and pays on time, which is more than I can say for two of the top three. What worries me is that the company also sells direct to my clients' peers; until that rule is written down, I place the easy cases here and the strategic ones elsewhere.

roster.name: Key partner
roster.rationale: Platform partner statements on the category are indirect.
roster.view: For my individual line this is a growth source I do not have to pay for, so I want the enrollment feed clean and the premium on time. For my small-group line it is a leak. I will partner where it grows individual and quietly resist where it cannibalizes group.

phases.summary: Financial confirmed recurring per-employer revenue from the board deck but found that the plan assumes partner-channel growth the company has not yet delivered. Market & Competitive could not corroborate the market-size figure in the deck from any third party and recorded a gap. Regulatory & Policy found that the individual-market pending federal rule pending this quarter is load-bearing for the employee-side economics.
notable: The partner-channel assumption and the pending federal rule together account for most of the plan's growth.
Only vendor-published market sizing exists for the sub-segment.

phases.summary: The Channel partner rated the product well on operations but named channel conflict as the reason it withholds strategic accounts, contesting Financial's partner-growth assumption. The Key partner split by line of business: partner for individual, resist for small group.
notable: Channel conflict surfaced independently from two seats.

phases.summary: The Adversary's most credible move was a white-label offer to the company's two largest platform partners within twelve months. The Evidence Auditor downgraded the market-size finding to open and asked the principal to supply the deck's source.
notable: Auditor downgrade widened the confidence band by three points.

evidence.claim: Recurring revenue per employer group, FY2025 and H1 2026, per board deck.
Plan assumes partner-channel enrollments triple in FY2027.
Sub-segment market size figure cited in the deck appears only in a vendor report.
Individual-market pending federal rule pending; agency statement dated 2026-08-15.
Three reseller forum threads in 2026 cite direct sales by the company as a reason to withhold accounts.

findings.statement: The FY2027 plan depends on partner-channel enrollments tripling; the company has not yet shown partner-channel growth at that rate.

contested_by.note: Partners will not scale while the company sells direct against them.

findings.so_what: Growth runway rests on a channel the company is currently in conflict with.

findings.statement: The market-size figure in the board deck cannot be corroborated outside a single vendor report.
findings.so_what: Share claims are unverifiable until a bottom-up sizing exists.

findings.statement: A pending federal pending federal rule determines whether employee-side economics hold for the lower-wage segment the plan targets.
findings.so_what: Regulatory driver is binary on a dated decision inside the horizon.

findings.statement: Resellers rate the product well operationally but withhold strategic accounts because the company sells direct to employers.
findings.so_what: Channel conflict is the largest self-inflicted drag on value proposition.
findings.question: choose_or_leave

findings.statement: Platform partners' individual-market leaders would partner; small-group leaders would resist.
findings.so_what: Platform partner relationships will be line-of-business specific.
findings.question: lands

findings.statement: As the incumbent, I offer the company's two largest platform partners a white-label deal within twelve months.

conflicts.description: Partner-channel growth: plan assumption vs. channel-partner behavior.

rulings.decision: Demoted to open pending the principal supplying the deck's market-size source.
rulings.rationale: Single T3 source; the Evidence Auditor could not resolve the locator to an independent figure.

judgment_calls.question: Should the council treat the direct-to-employer channel as strategic (keep) or as a conflict to be resolved in favor of partners? The score moves roughly six points between the two readings.
judgment_calls.why_principal: This is a board strategy choice, not an evidence question.

judgment_calls.question: Please supply the source for the market-size figure on p.9 of the board deck.
judgment_calls.why_principal: Only the principal has access to management's source.

handoffs.item: Test whether partners will scale at the rate the plan assumes.
handoffs.why: Financial cannot judge channel intent from the deck.

gaps.expected: Independent market sizing for the sub-segment.
gaps.why_expected: Segment is large enough for analyst coverage.
gaps.principal_could_supply: Management's source for the deck figure

open_questions.question: What is the written rule on which employers the company will and will not sell to directly?

drivers.name: Competitive standing
drivers.rationale: Position is real but share is unverifiable (F-002 open).

drivers.name: Value proposition strength
drivers.rationale: Operationally strong with channel-partners; channel conflict caps it.

drivers.name: Operating quality and execution
drivers.rationale: Payments and quoting praised; plan delivery unproven.

drivers.name: Growth runway
drivers.rationale: Runway rests on partners the company is in conflict with; incumbent can pre-empt.

drivers.name: Regulatory and policy tailwind
drivers.rationale: Binary on a dated federal decision.

drivers.name: Capital and exit optionality
drivers.rationale: Consolidating segment with multiple buyer types.

assessment.verdict: Sample Co is a well-run administrator whose growth case is held hostage by its own channel strategy. Channel partners like the product and dislike competing with it; the plan's partner-channel growth will not arrive until that is resolved. The pending federal rule sets the ceiling on the lower-wage segment. If the board resolves the channel question in favor of partners and the pending federal rule goes the company's way, the score moves into the high 60s; if neither, into the 40s.
assessment.biggest_stakeholder_risk: Channel partner: strategic accounts withheld until the direct-sales rule is written.
what_would_raise: A written channel rule and evidence partners are scaling
Independent market sizing (principal: supply the deck's source)
assessment.confidence_rationale: One headline demoted; one load-bearing gap open; capital driver rests on fewer than two findings.
assessment.standing_summary: A credible mid-tier administrator in a consolidating segment; share unverified.
assessment.positioning_summary: Operationally differentiated with channel-partners; positioning undermined by channel conflict.
assessment.operating_summary: Strong payments and quoting; plan delivery and partner scaling unproven.
assessment.label: Probability of value creation over 3–5 years
